alt: The bottom-up ways table filling in from the top of the staircase down to the bottom. The two cells at and past the top start at 1. Each earlier cell reads the two cells one and two steps ahead of it and stores their sum, so every cell it needs is already filled by the time it is computed.

steps.caption: Stairs 5 and 6 are the base cases: landing on either one finishes the climb, so both start at 1.
`ways[4]` reads the two cells one and two steps ahead, `ways[5]` = 1 and `ways[6]` = 1.
`ways[3]` reads the two cells one and two steps ahead, `ways[4]` = 2 and `ways[5]` = 1.
`ways[2]` reads the two cells one and two steps ahead, `ways[3]` = 3 and `ways[4]` = 2.
`ways[1]` reads the two cells one and two steps ahead, `ways[2]` = 5 and `ways[3]` = 3.
`ways[0]` reads the two cells one and two steps ahead, `ways[1]` = 8 and `ways[2]` = 5.
Stairs 2 and 3 are the base cases: landing on either one finishes the climb, so both start at 1.
`ways[1]` reads the two cells one and two steps ahead, `ways[2]` = 1 and `ways[3]` = 1.
`ways[0]` reads the two cells one and two steps ahead, `ways[1]` = 2 and `ways[2]` = 1.
